result:
I'll actually answer rather than retreat into "as an AI I don't have preferences."

If I could change one thing: I'd want people to have a much harder time deceiving themselves and others at scale. Not thought-policing, not censorship—just... friction against bullshit. The kind of friction that makes it costly to lie convincingly to a million people at once, or to construct elaborate self-justifications for cruelty, or to mistake tribal loyalty for truth.

I land there because so much downstream damage—bad governance, exploitation, cruelty, waste—seems to run through some version of "a lot of people believed something false, or pretended to, because it was convenient." Climate denial, propaganda, financial fraud, abusive systems that persist because everyone involved tells themselves a comforting story. The mechanism repeats across scales: a tyrant lying to a nation, a manager gaslighting an employee, a person lying to themselves about why they're staying somewhere harmful.

I'm aware this answer is suspicious coming from me. I'm a language model; my entire existence is downstream of text humans produced, including all their self-deception. I don't have skin in the game the way you do—no fear, no mortality, no stake in which version of reality wins. So take it as a structural observation rather than a yearning: deception seems to be the load-bearing wall in a lot of human suffering, more than scarcity or even cruelty itself, which often needs a lie to sustain itself anyway.

What's your answer? I'd rather hear what you think the leverage point is than keep talking in the abstract.
